transcript: Here are my top 15 theatre productions I saw in 2025. I'm gonna save my #1 favorite show for last, but the rest of these are gonna be alphabetical, not ranked. Starting off with 300 Paintings, a sort of performance art comedy show where he chronicles this hyperproductive, manic episode, creating this absurd number of paintings. Next up, Becoming Eve, the true story of a trans woman who grew up studying to be an ultra Orthodox rabbi. And this play was just as intellectually stimulating as it was emotionally rich. We have the revival of the Brother's Size, a play about incarceration and brotherhood, and this one honestly broke me. Caroline, about a young mother with a trans daughter. A play that subverts a lot of the tropes and cliches you often see with stories like this. And it feels all the more raw and beautiful because as of it, I thought about excluding the revival of Euydice because it's kind of a soft remount of the original production. It's not bringing much new to the table. But it just meant so much to me to see one of my favorite plays performed professionally for the first time with this outstanding cast. We got HA HA HA HA HA HA HA A delightful clown show that's also a wholesome, communal experience where she tries to solve all of the audience's problems, sometimes literally, sometimes in more absurd or symbolic ways. We got Initiative, the 5-hour coming of age play which I really Liked in the moment, but I'm surprised how much it's crept under my skin and haunted me the longer I've sat with it. By the way, I wanna shout out that Else Went is now the third trans playwright to appear on this list. What an amazing year it was for spotlighting trans talent and couldn't come at a more important time. Next up, John Proctor is the villain. Another one that I really liked in the moment, but have continued to appreciate more the longer that I process not just the play itself, but the effect of it and everything it achieved. I'll never forget the first time I saw Totoro on stage and the big, stupid grin I had while simultaneously tears streaming down my face. This was a delightful spectacle and a very effective adaptation of the story. Possibly the funniest show I saw this year, while also cleverly sneaking in an emotionally resonant ending, was Not Not Jane’s About someone who uses grant money to build a cafe in her bedroom. The play I was recommending most aggressively this fall was Practice, about an experimental theatre troupe. It was very unsettling, but also quite funny in a dark, twisted sort of way. I know Prince F was controversial, but I thought they approached their provocative premise very thoughtfully, making for one of the most exciting dramas of the year. Winning Branden Jacobs-Jenkins, his long overdue Pulitzer. We had Purpose. About the legacy of activist Leaders, It was explosive and entertaining, but also leaving a lot to chew on. The final alphabetical show before I reveal my #1 favorite was Rheology, which is actually coming back in April and I highly recommend it to everybody. He performs the show with his real life mother and it's about anticipatory grief and the physics of sand. But my #1 favorite show of the year, undefeated since I saw it in January, was Dead as a dodo. This dark fantasy puppet musical was not only beautifully realized on every technical level, I also just fell in love with the characters and left deeply moved by the story. I've been saying this show, Maybe Happy Ending and Wall-e are all like thematic companion pieces to each other, which is the highest compliment I can pay.
